The 30 drawings cover these subsystems:

| Subsystem | Drawings | Count |
|---|---|---:|
| Box / enclosure | D-001–D-005 | 5 |
| Powder handling | D-006–D-010 | 5 |
| Recoater | D-011–D-015 | 5 |
| Optics | D-016–D-020 | 5 |
| Gas flow | D-021–D-022 | 2 |
| Build plate | D-023–D-028 | 6 |
| Z-axis | D-029–D-030 | 2 |
| **Total** |  | **30** |

D-006, the canister wall drawing, is counted under powder handling.

The BOM has **two Z-related groups**:

### Explicitly named Z-axis rows (SensorGantry family)
- Z axis linear rod
- Z axis stepper bracket
- Z axis linear stepper
- Z axis guide clamp
- Z axis linear guide

The drawings include **D-029, “Z-axis BottomPlate,”** and **D-030, “Z-axis MotorPlate.”** The BOM has no row named “BottomPlate”; D-030 may relate to the **Z axis stepper bracket**, but the documents don’t establish that match explicitly. The rod, stepper, guide clamp, and linear guide have no matching drawings in the supplied set.

### Build-platform lift components
The BOM’s **Build-plate** family is also part of the machine’s Z-axis assembly. Drawings are provided for:
- Build cylinder — **D-023**
- Build base — **D-024**
- Seal clamp plate / build-base ring — **D-025**
- Build Plate — **D-026**
- Build cylinder clamp ring — **D-027**
- Heating element plate — **D-028**

Other Build-plate rows—including the ceramic seal, motor plate shaft, motors, drivers, heating elements, and thermocouple plate—have no clear matching drawing among D-001–D-030.

The fabrication drawings show these custom parts for the recoater:

- **Recoater arm** (D-011), for the linear bushing
- **Recoater mount block** (D-012), the mounting block for the linear guide
- **Recoater plate** (D-013), the adjustment plate
- **Recoater linear plate** (D-014), the plate for the linear guide
- **Silicone wipers** (D-015), two 1 mm-thick pieces

These are the drawn custom parts; the drawings don’t provide a complete list of the recoater’s standard hardware.
Drawing D-014, **RecoaterStagePlate.pdf** (titled “Recoater Linear Plate”).
Drawing D-010 documents the BOM row **Powder stepper bracket**.

**D-030** is the motor plate drawing: it is titled “Z-axis MotorPlate.” D-029 is titled “Z-axis BottomPlate.” The BOM doesn’t directly link a drawing to its “Motor plate” entry, so this identification is based on the drawing titles.

**Partly.** The BOM lists both doors as aluminium, and drawing D-001 specifies two 3 mm aluminium doors with through-holes, consistent with the BOM’s note that the holes were not threaded.

It does not distinguish the front door’s window, seal and handle from the back door, which the BOM describes as having none of those features. So the drawing agrees on the basic door material and hole style, but doesn’t document the BOM’s front/back differences.

The BOM lists the Build Plate material as **“Stainless steel, Steel.”** Drawing D-026 specifies **AISI 316 stainless-steel sheet**, but its note also says “stainless and alu” and calls for 1–3 of each.

So they **partly agree**: both identify stainless steel, but the drawing also mentions aluminium, which the BOM does not list.

The silicone parts/materials listed are:

- **Recoater Blade** — silicone sheet; the drawing specifies a 1 mm silicone wiper.
- **Silicone gasket f-theta ring** — silicone; the drawing specifies a 1 mm silicone gasket.
- **Tri-Clamp silicone gasket** — silicone sealing gasket.
- **Silicone sheet** — raw material for making gaskets.

The BOM also lists **DOWSIL 7091 silicone sealant**, but that is a consumable rather than a fabricated part.

That figure includes the listed purchased items and the two doors at DKK 100 each. It **doesn’t capture the cost of several custom-made Box parts**, which are entered as DKK 0 or have no cost recorded—such as the side panels, top, print platform, window frame, and bracing. It also excludes any unrecorded fabrication or assembly labor.

It’s the **aluminium threaded block** that connects the recoater stage plate to the arm. The drawing specifies **EN-AW 5005 aluminium**, an overall length of **120 mm**, and **M6 threaded holes**.
The heating element plate is **2–3 mm thick** (shown as 3.0 / 2.0 on drawing D-028).

It’s a flat annular aluminium ring: **Ø250 mm outer diameter**, **Ø224 mm inner diameter**, with **8 × Ø3.4 mm through-holes**, each countersunk **Ø6.9 mm × 90°**. The drawing specifies EN-AW 5005 aluminium and calls out **3.0 / 2.0 mm**; this view is illustrative, not a dimensionally exact model.
Corrected: **Build Plate — Aluminum**, not stainless steel. The BOM and drawing D-026 currently specify stainless steel, so those material callouts should be updated.

The BOM lists the **Omron S8VK-C48024 (24 VDC, 20 A)** from **RS Components**: [RS product page](https://dk.rs-online.com/web/p/din-skinnemonterbare-stromforsyninger/7866462). It doesn’t list another supplier.
No. The BOM lists one source for the laser: Max Photonics, model MFSC-300W. It doesn’t identify an alternate supplier.
The BOM lists **DTU** as the supplier for the custom recoater mount block. The drawing specifies aluminium (EN-AW 5005).
The BOM lists **Misumi** as the supplier for the dispenser drum coupling (SCOC20-6-8). It doesn’t list another seller.

The cylinder clamp ring secures the build cylinder to the build platform. It also locates and holds the build-base and Z-axis motor assembly. The build cylinder drawing specifies a nominal 280 mm diameter; the clamp ring drawing shows a 264 mm bore, so the drawings appear to rely on a stepped or mating feature rather than the cylinder’s full outer diameter.

The recoater arm is **not directly connected to the build plate**. It attaches to the recoater mount block, which connects it to the recoater stage plate. That plate rides on the recoater’s linear bearings, supported by the recoater wall. The arm carries the recoater head and wiper across the build plate.

The **Print Platform** is the main interface between subsystems: its BOM design intent says it bridges the **Z-axis/build-plate**, **recoater**, and **powder-handling** subsystems, and that the shielding-gas cross-flow emerges from it.

| Subsystems connected | Connecting parts and role |
|---|---|
| **Box ↔ Build-plate / Z-axis** | The **Print Platform** is the stated bridge. The build assembly includes the **build cylinder clamp ring**, **build base**, **motor plate**, and **motor plate shaft**; the build-base drawing also shows mounting and alignment features. |
| **Box ↔ Recoater** | The **Print Platform** provides the interface to the recoater subsystem. Within the recoater assembly, the **Recoater Wall** holds the linear stage; the **stage plate**, **mount block**, **arm**, and **head** carry the wiper over the build area. |
| **Recoater ↔ Powder handling** | Powder is dispensed by the **powder hopper/canister and roller/dispenser components**, then spread across the build area by the **Recoater head** and **silicone wiper**. The BOM specifically describes the platform’s powder connection as being “via the recoater.” |
| **Gas flow ↔ Process chamber / Box** | The **gas-flow inlet geometry**, **end duct**, and **process-chamber inlet fitting** connect the gas system to the chamber. The **blower outlet** drawing specifies a flange through a machine wall; the blower, filters, tubing, valves, and oxygen sensor make up the associated gas path. |
| **Optics ↔ Box / Process chamber** | The **Galvo Box Bracket**, **galvo support brackets**, and **Sunny Galvo Adapter Plate** mount the galvo/collimator assembly to the enclosure’s top structure. The **F-theta seal ring** and silicone gasket seal the lens interface; the optical path then enters the process chamber. |
| **Electrical ↔ Powered subsystems** | The **electrical cabinet**, power supplies, wiring, connectors, and controls distribute power and control to the motors and drivers in the recoater, build-plate, powder, and gantry subsystems, as well as to the heaters/PID/SSR, gas valves and sensors, blower, and laser equipment. |

For the enclosure itself, the BOM explicitly lists the **Print Platform** as interfacing with the **Left Side Box**, **Back Box**, and **Right Box**; the **Front Side Box** also connects to the platform and carries the **Front Door**. The rest of the enclosure panels and top structure complete the box around these subsystem interfaces.
